proposal.hypothesis: With the fixed 128-thread CTA, each warp can reduce its lanes using the existing helper, while the final warp needs only shuffle-down offsets 2 and 1 to combine its four warp totals. This targeted final combine may reduce CTA-local work versus a general 32-lane reduction, but the measured candidates suggest that any local change may be masked by complete-run costs. The launch geometry, one-value-per-lane loading, stage schedule, scratch selection, and final copy stay fixed so the controller can test the local change independently of topology.

retained: Replace reduce0's modulo-based shared-memory tree with one warp-local reduction per warp, followed by a single CTA barrier.
Use the existing warpReduceSum helper for lane reductions, then combine the four warp totals using only shuffle-down offsets 2 and 1 in warp 0.
Load one value per lane and use zero for out-of-range tail lanes; preserve the 128-thread launch, multi-stage scratch schedule, scratch selection, and final copy.
